subject: english-language
title: Grice and the Cooperative Mind
welcome_lead: Why do we say less than we mean — and still understand each other? Enter Grice's elegant calculus of implicature.
meta_desc: Grice's maxims, the cooperative principle and implicature at A-Level English Language.
final_note: You have unlocked Grice — the rules we break to mean more than we say.

concepts.def: H. P. Grice (1975) — speakers cooperate in conversation, making contributions that fit the accepted purpose of the exchange.
Make your contribution as informative as required, no more, no less.
Do not say what you believe to be false or for which you lack evidence.
Be clear, brief, orderly; avoid obscurity and ambiguity.
Meaning inferred when a maxim is flouted — listeners reason about why the speaker broke it.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Grice argued that beneath the surface of conversation lies a cooperative principle. Speakers follow four maxims — Quantity, Quality, Relation and Manner.

When apparent violations occur, listeners assume the speaker is still cooperating at a deeper level, generating implicature.

Asked Is John a good worker? a reply of He shows up on time flouts Quantity — too little for praise. The implicature: John is not very good.

Irony, metaphor and politeness all rely on this gap between what is said and what is meant.

Critics note that cultures differ in how directly they value maxims, and that politeness theories (Brown & Levinson) often subsume Grice.

Yet the framework remains the foundation for understanding inference in talk.

mcqs.q: Conversational implicature arises when a speaker:
options: Flouts a maxim
Obeys all maxims fully
Whispers
Switches language
The assumption that speakers cooperate in conversation by following maxims of quantity, quality, relation and manner — flouting these creates implicature.
The cooperative principle means people are always nice to each other.
Implicature is a kind of grammatical mistake.
The cooperative principle means everyone must agree in conversation.
The cooperative principle means everyone must agree in conversation.
Implicature is a kind of grammatical mistake.
Implicature is the same as the literal meaning of a sentence.
Meaning conveyed beyond what is literally said — generated when speakers obey or deliberately flout Grice's maxims. 'Some students passed' implicates 'not all', via the maxim of quantity.

mcqs.q: What is an adjacency pair in conversation analysis?
options: Adjacency pairs are two people who sit next to each other while talking.
A two-part sequence where the first part conditions the second — question/answer, greeting/greeting, request/acceptance-or-refusal. The second part is 'conditionally relevant' on the first.
Adjacency pairs are pairs of synonyms in vocabulary lists.
Implicature is a kind of grammatical mistake.
